title: A master's in finance in Germany
description: Where to study finance in Germany, what the programmes require, what they cost and which careers they lead to.
html:
Germany is home to Europe's largest financial centre after London and to a dense banking, insurance and corporate finance sector, which makes a master's in finance here a practical choice. Most programmes are taught in English and several are at public universities with no tuition.

What the programmes cover

A typical two-year master's combines corporate finance, asset pricing, financial econometrics and risk management with electives in banking, fintech or sustainable finance. Business schools emphasise case work and internships; university programmes lean more towards quantitative methods and research.

Where to study

Frankfurt's business schools and university sit next to the banks and offer the strongest recruiting pipeline. The universities in Mannheim, Munich, Cologne and Berlin have well-regarded finance departments, and several universities of applied sciences offer more practice-oriented programmes with compulsory internships.

Admission requirements

A bachelor's degree in business, economics or a quantitative subject with a good final grade; an English certificate; often a GMAT or GRE score, especially at business schools; a letter of motivation and a CV. Deadlines for the winter semester usually fall between January and May.

Tuition

Public universities charge only the semester contribution, apart from Baden-Württemberg's €1,500 per semester for non-EU students. Private business schools charge between €15,000 and €40,000 for the whole programme, with scholarships for strong candidates.

Alternatives

If a pure finance programme feels narrow, consider management with a finance track, financial engineering, economics with a finance focus or accounting and taxation. Each keeps the door to finance roles open while broadening the options.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need German? Not for the programme, but it helps for jobs at German banks and insurers. What do graduates earn? Starting salaries in banking and consulting in Frankfurt typically start around €55,000 to €70,000. Can I work during the degree? Yes, up to 20 hours a week during term, and internships are common between semesters.
